reviews.title: Schlechtes UX-Design oder bewusste Kundentäuschung?
reviews.text: Wir haben uns gefreut, dass die Lidl Plus App ein „kostenloses Brot aus der Selbstbedienung Theke“ bei einem Einkauf von über 25 € versprach. Bei einem Einkauf von über 90 € ist mir dann durch Zufall aufgefallen, dass uns das Brot berechnet wurde. Als ich die Kassiererin darauf ansprach, wurde ich gefragt, wo die Information des kostenloses Brotes stehen würde. Ich zeigte ihr das in meiner App. Während Sie fast 1 Minute lang auf meinem Handy in meiner App rumklickte, um diese Information zu überprüfen, wurde die Schlange an der Kasse hinter mir immer länger. Schließlich zeigte sie mir, dass in der App an irgendeiner Stelle eine zusätzliche Information hinterlegt war, dass nicht ein Brot, sondern nur bestimmte Brote bei einem Einkauf von über 25 € mitgenommen werden dürften. Mein Fazit zu dieser App ist, dass entweder die App ein miserables Benutzer Interface hat oder dass Lidl ganz bewusst ihre Kunden hier in die Irre führt. So oder so gibt es von mir nur einen Stern für diese App.

Lidl Plus étant désormais une carte de fidélité exclusivement dématérialisée, les clients dont le téléphone ne peut pas installer la dernière version de l’application à cause des exigences de logiciel se retrouvent privés d’accès à leur compte, à leurs coupons et à leurs avantages de fidélité.

Le problème est particulièrement contestable pour les clients qui étaient déjà inscrits : ce n’est pas leur téléphone qui a cessé de fonctionner, c’est l’évolution du service Lidl Plus qui les empêche désormais d’y accéder.

Le Code de la consommation encadre précisément les services numériques, notamment leur conformité, leur compatibilité et les conséquences des mises à jour lorsqu’elles affectent l’accès ou l’utilisation du service.

On peut donc légitimement s’interroger sur la conformité de cette pratique lorsqu’aucune solution alternative n’est proposée aux clients concernés…

Est-il réellement acceptable qu’un client perde l’accès à des avantages de fidélité qu’il a acquis simplement parce que son téléphone, pourtant encore parfaitement fonctionnel, n’est plus compatible avec la nouvelle application ?

C’est une pratique dont la légalité pose sérieusement question…

Parce que fidéliser ses clients ne devrait pas signifier leur imposer un nouveau téléphone!!

reviews.title: Previous was better
reviews.text:
I’m sorry to say this, but the previous version of the app was significantly better.

To start with, when you go to the promotions section—for example, the ice cream deals—and open the details to see which products are included, you only see the product names without any pictures. In the previous version, there were images, which made it much easier to know exactly which product was included. Now, you’re often left unsure whether you’re actually looking at the right item.

Previously, you could get 3–6 free items and choose exactly what you wanted. Now, the system has been replaced with points, where 1 point equals $1 spent. Unfortunately, the number of points required for the rewards feels completely disproportionate to what you actually get in return.

What’s even more disappointing is that for an entire month, the same items have been available in the points promotion, without any changes or new options. Nothing else seems to be discounted or offered as an alternative.

Overall, I feel that the new version of the app was launched too early and is still quite underdeveloped. The previous version was much more user-friendly, rewarding, and enjoyable to use. I really hope these issues are addressed because, at the moment, the new system feels like a significant step backward.

I doubt your other customers would have the forethought to save a screenshot of the card, so please just add a button to save your Lidl Plus Card to the iPhone Wallet, just like other supermarkets! Thanks! (I finally got 2 cellular signal bars after I exited your store, so there was some area outage! Since you have no control over this, it’s important for you to add a Wallet card option!)

You can’t discover what the store stocks, let alone stock availability. You can’t check which products have become obsolete and are no longer available. All you can do is collect points (allowing Lidl insight into your shopping habits and therefore be at a better position to exploit you through such knowledge) and to bring to your attention whichever products they currently wish to hype. This app is a thinly veiled, an extremely thinly veiled means to track the customers’ behaviour and therefore discover how best to exploit us. Sainsbury’s app lets you see what they stock as does Aldi’s, Morrisons’, Asda’s, Boots, Argos’, Superdrug’s and ToolStation’s. reviews.title: La app che faceva la differenza
reviews.text: Il nuovo piano di accumulo punti sembra una presa in giro. Che detta così può sembrare provocatoria. Ma non è così. Il coupon che, raggiunta la soglia di spesa mensile  dava piccoli, siamo d’accordo, regali o sconti. Oggi facendo 2 calcoli per avere uno sconto di 10 euro devo spendere 1000 euro. E che sconto sarebbe? Che premio è? A chi potrebbe fare gola? Prima invece, a parte i coupon intermedi che ti davano diritto ad alcuni seppur economici articoli gratis, potevi contare, al raggiungimento della soglia di spesa di 250 euro mensili, su uno sconto del 5% che ti giocavi un po’ come volevi. Non è il 5% o le 10 euro ma queste app sono utili se chi le usa intravvede la possibilità di poter risparmiare. Col nuovo sistema, per intravvedere qualcosa, devi avere il telescopio quantico. Visto che per avere 10 miseri euro di sconto potresti dover aspettare mediamente dai 3 ai 5 mesi.

Il faudrait absolument mettre en place un système qui permette d’utiliser la carte fidélité sans que celle-ci ne soit liée à l’identité réelle du client. Il y en a marre d’avoir toutes nos données en ligne. Ça ouvre grand la porte à des systèmes de surveillance généralisée comme dans les scénarios de science fiction dystopiques ou comme le crédit social en Chine. Et en plus il suffirait d’un seul hack pour qu’on sache tout ce que j’ai acheté chez Lidl depuis des années et où exactement, c’est trop de données emmagasinées. Il ne faut pas habituer les gens à donner toutes leurs données comme ça. Un bon compromis : garder le système de fidélité mais le rendre lié à un identifiant non nominatif. Faites en votre nouvelle pub : LIDL protège votre vie privée et grâce à LIDL le futur ne sera pas comme 1984. Montrez l’exemple. Et comme ça vous auriez encore toutes les données statistiques dont vous avez besoin pour optimisez vos prix et offres.

reviews.title: Didn’t expect that!
reviews.text:
Came into the Wantage store after a very busy day at a bit after 19:00hrs. 
I was intrigued in the deal for a pizza, garlic bread and dip for £6.00 but when I looked on the shelves, there were plenty of pizzas and dips, but no garlic bread of any sort from the deal. I went to a staff member and said, “Excuse me “ politely and he completely ignored me. I spoke again and asked if there were any garlic bread anywhere else or if there were any alternative options. He said, “No, if they’re gone, the deal isn’t there.” But then added with a grin, “It’s your fault if you leave it this late to do your shopping “
I actually didn’t register that at the time, or I’d have had a few more words for him. But he made me feel like he didn’t want to be there and that he took it out on me. 
He made an assumption that I had the choice of when I “decided” to go shopping!
If your store is open until 22:00hrs, I’d appreciate that your staff don’t make judgements about what time I’m in there and if the deal is showing on the App, then I’d hope for all the stock to be there to honour the advertised deal. If the stock isn’t there, I’d hope the technology was there to take the deal off the app.
I had no issues with any other staff there and gave generally been delighted with their attitude, but this particular person does not seem suited to your store and he’s bringing down the great work of the others!
Very disappointed for once.

reviews.title: Annoying hindsight app!
reviews.text:
There’s nothing quite so annoying as having an app that’s supposed to give you money off your shopping (and other offers), but in practice just tells you that you could have saved money a few days ago, but missed the opportunity because you have a life outside of Lidl, and your shopping habits don’t revolve around Lidl offers!

Give me an offer that I don’t have to activate to receive… I get it automatically when I next shop. Give it a reasonable ‘shelf life’ so if I’m busy and don’t shop in Lidl every few days, I don’t miss out. Give me offers on things I actually want, rather than random things I don’t need or want. Here’s a radical idea… just give me a small percentage off the shopping I actually want to buy from you, and don’t give me any ‘special offers’ at all… they’re mostly just really annoying!

reviews.title: Too Many Updates, Constant Logouts, Broken Password Recovery
reviews.text:
The app needs updates far too often, and after updating it frequently logs me out. The worst part is when I’m in the store and need it most: it suddenly forces an update, won’t let me log in, and I can’t activate and use my coupons/discounts. Very inconvenient and not user-friendly. Please reduce the number of updates, and if you do update, make sure users don’t have to log in again.

Also I registered with my phone number, but now the app forces email login and the recovery flow is broken— it sends a code and asks me to enter it while simultaneously saying I’ve reached an internal limit, so I can’t restore access at all.
